title: Vector and Particle Lab
description: A two-mode p5.js physics lab: in One ball mode, labeled position, velocity and gravity arrows and a draggable second ball separate the roles of the three vectors and of collision detection (dist < r1 + r2) versus collision response; in Fountain mode, a particle system applies one rule to many particles that fade with their remaining life.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: p5.js
Vectors
Physics Simulation
Collision Detection
Particle Systems
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

educational.topic: Vectors, Euler integration, collisions and particle systems in p5.js
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish the roles of position, velocity, and acceleration vectors, and of collision detection versus collision response, by changing parameters and observing the labeled arrows.
prerequisites: The Vectors, Physics Simulation, Collision Detection and Particle System sections of Chapter 6

controls.label: Reset
controls.action: Restart the ball and clear the particles

canvasInteractions: Drag the fixed ball into the moving ball's path (One ball mode)

simulation.modelType: Physics simulation (Euler integration) and particle system
equations: collision detected when dist(center1, center2) < r1 + r2
response: v = v - (1 + e)(v . n) n, with n the unit contact normal and e the bounciness
assumptions: One frame is one time step
The fixed ball does not move when hit
limitations: Euler integration gains or loses a little energy per step
Particles do not collide with each other

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided exploration: change one parameter, observe which arrow or readout changes
keyQuestions: Which arrow changes length when you move the gravity slider, and which does not?
When the balls overlap while paused, has a collision been detected? Has it been responded to?
Why do all particles follow the same rule yet look different?
commonMisconceptions: Velocity and acceleration always point the same way
Detecting a collision automatically changes the motion
Gravity changes position directly rather than through velocity
assessmentOpportunities: Explain the difference between detection and response using the readout
Predict the arrows at the top of a bounce
